- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at 1-2% above recent peak for next 3-5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below 65–68), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0 point lag correction for next 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights recent sentiment spikes; weight sentiment from last 7 days more heavily than last 18 for correction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.00, +0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; apply smoothing filter to sentiment before forecasting.
- When true outcome deviates >3% from 30d forecast, check if sentiment was neutral or negative 3 days prior — if so, model likely missed a reversal; adjust downward by 1–2 points.
